title: Syntax vs. Semantics: How Transformers Learn Deep Dependencies
abstract: arXiv:2608.26139v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language Models demonstrate remarkable syntactic fluency, yet the optimization dynamics governing their acquisition of deep semantic dependencies remain poorly understood. We propose a mechanistic framework that models this learning process as a competition between Surface Statistics and Deep Semantics. Our theoretical analysis identifies a ``Gradient Starvation" phenomenon where the error signals for sparse semantic dependencies are actively suppressed during early optimization. This suppression impedes the learning of structural reasoning and causes its emergence to manifest as a sudden phase transition. Furthermore, this framework offers a mechanistic basis for the effectiveness of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) strategies. By externalizing intermediate reasoning steps into concrete tokens, CoT effectively bypasses the suppression regime inherent to implicit reasoning. translated_title: 语法与语义：Transformer如何学习深层依赖关系
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型展现出显著的句法流畅性，但其获取深层语义依赖关系的优化动力学仍然知之甚少。我们提出一个机制性框架，将该学习过程建模为表面统计与深层语义之间的竞争。我们的理论分析识别出一种“梯度饥饿”现象，即在早期优化过程中，稀疏语义依赖的错误信号被主动抑制。这种抑制阻碍了结构推理的学习，并导致其出现表现为突然的相变。此外，该框架为思维链（CoT）策略的有效性提供了机制性基础。通过将中间推理步骤外化为具体标记，CoT有效绕过了隐式推理固有的抑制机制。我们在从玩具变换器到不同规模的实验中验证了这些发现。
tldr: 该论文提出一个机制框架，揭示Transformer学习深层语义依赖时存在“梯度饥饿”现象，并解释了思维链策略如何通过外化推理步骤绕过该抑制机制。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a mechanistic framework revealing a "Gradient Starvation" phenomenon in how Transformers learn deep semantic dependencies, and explains how Chain-of-Thought bypasses this suppression by externalizing reasoning steps.
